newsitem.title: HONG KONG: S&P raises China senior debt rating to BBB-plus.
newsitem.headline: S&P raises China senior debt rating to BBB-plus.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Wednesday it has raised its issuer credit rating and senior unsecured debt rating for China to BBB-plus from BBB, and had affirmed its A-2 short-term foreign currency credit rating.
The rating agency also said it had revised its outlook on China to stable from positive.

The upgrade reflected the recent gradual advancement in and good prospects for extending reforms during the next several years, and considerable external financial flexibility, S&P said in a statement.
It also reflected an expectation of China's continuing long-term record of exceptionally high savings and investment rates, robust growth, manageable inflation and strong external performance.

However, China's credit worthiness remained constrained by uncertain though large economic and political costs associated with reforming state enterprises, social security and the state banks, the incomplete status of fiscal and monetary reforms, and an inflexible political system, S&P said.
